titulo: Authorization: OAuth with iss (RFC 9207), minimum scope, secret kept out of the repo
lead: An HTTP server on the internet without a token is an open tool for anyone. In MCP, your server is an OAuth resource server: it doesn't issue tokens, it only checks them. In this lesson you protect the kit's server, see the 401 that starts the client's login, and give each token only the scope it needs.
objetivo: protect the HTTP server with a token: 401 with metadata, minimum scope per tool, and secret kept out of the repository.

aprende.t: Who issues (authorization server) and who checks (your MCP server)
401 with WWW-Authenticate and the RFC 9728 document
Scope for the whole server and scope per tool (403 insufficient_scope)
iss (RFC 9207) and credential bound to the issuer: what belongs to the client

hero_alt: Keychain with two keys of different colors and a blank badge on a dark table, a server door in the background.

secoes.titulo: From the 401 to the token with the right scope

nos.detalhe: The client calls the server without Authorization.
The server answers 401 with resource_metadata: the URL of the resource's RFC 9728 document.
The document says which authorization server issues tokens for this resource and which scopes exist.

The client does the OAuth flow with the authorization server (your IdP). On the way back, it checks the iss parameter (RFC 9207) to be sure the response came from the right issuer. That is the client's job.
Your server verifies the token (signature, expiry exp, audience aud = this server) and the scopes. Missing scope: 403 insufficient_scope.

secoes.legenda: In SDK v2 2.3.1, iss validation and the credential bound to the issuer are client-side options (finishAuth); the server is the resource server.

secoes.sub: Rehearsal: two tokens come from environment variables. In production, swap the verifier for your IdP's JWT check.

secoes.titulo: No token, read token, reservation token
secoes.sub: The block generates two random tokens just for this run and calls the server three times.

blocos.conteudo:
cd ~/projetos/formacao-webmcp-mcp-v72/kit
export TOKEN_LEITURA=$(openssl rand -hex 16) TOKEN_RESERVA=$(openssl rand -hex 16)
node http-auth.mjs & PID=$!; sleep 1
echo "## sem token"
curl -s -o /dev/null -D - -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3334/mcp \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' | grep -i -e '^HTTP' -e '^www-authenticate'
echo "## metadados do recurso (RFC 9728)"
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3334/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp; echo
echo "## token de leitura"; TOKEN=$TOKEN_LEITURA node teste-auth.mjs
echo "## token de reserva"; TOKEN=$TOKEN_RESERVA node teste-auth.mjs
kill $PID; wait $PID 2>/dev/null

abas.html:
turmas (com token): http://127.0.0.1:3334/mcp
## sem token
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token", error_description="Missing Authorization header", scope="turmas:ler", resource_metadata="http://127.0.0.1:3334/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp"
## metadados do recurso (RFC 9728)
{"resource":"http://127.0.0.1:3334/mcp","authorization_servers":["https://auth.exemplo.com"],"scopes_supported":["turmas:ler","turmas:reservar"]}
## token de leitura
buscar_turmas: ok
reservar_vaga: recusado (Insufficient scope: required "turmas:reservar")
## token de reserva
buscar_turmas: ok
reservar_vaga: reservado: html-01 para aluno@exemplo.com (restam 2)

The read token gets past the server's gate (scope turmas:ler) but cannot reserve: it lacks turmas:reservar. That is the minimum scope working per tool.

texto: Token, signing key, and client secret come from an environment variable or a vault. The kit refuses to start without TOKEN_LEITURA and TOKEN_RESERVA.
Put the .env file in .gitignore before the first commit. Before publishing, search: git grep -n -i "token\|secret" -- ':!*.md'.
expectedResource makes the server accept only tokens issued for it. Without it, a token from another service on the same IdP would get through.
One scope per type of action. Read and reserve separate; an agent that only looks things up gets read-only.

secoes.sub: The kit's gate and your service's gate.

exercicios.pronto: HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized without a token; with the read token, reservar_vaga: recusado (Insufficient scope: required "turmas:reservar"); with the reservation token, reservar_vaga: reservado.

exercicios.texto: Run node http-auth.mjs; echo "saída: $?" in a terminal without the variables.
exercicios.pronto: defina TOKEN_LEITURA e TOKEN_RESERVA no ambiente e saída: 2.

exercicios.texto: In mapa-mcp.md, list one scope per tool that has consequences, and add scopeChallenge: requireScopes(...) to them.
exercicios.pronto: grep -c "requireScopes" servidor.mjs → equal to the number of tools with consequences.

perguntas.p: In MCP OAuth, what is the role of your MCP server?
opcoes: Client, which logs the user in
Resource server, which checks the token
Proxy between the model and the IdP
perguntas.explica: The authorization server (IdP) issues the token. The MCP server checks the signature, expiry, audience, and scopes.

perguntas.p: What does the server's 401 give the client so it can start the login?
opcoes: The ready-made access token in the response body, to reuse
The WWW-Authenticate header with the URL of the RFC 9728 metadata
The user's encrypted password, for the client to check again
A link to download the SDK
perguntas.explica: The resource_metadata points to the document that says which authorization server to use and which scopes exist.

perguntas.p: Where does the validation of the iss parameter (RFC 9207) happen?
opcoes: In the client, when the login returns
In the MCP server, on every call
In the model, when it picks the tool
perguntas.explica: iss protects the client from accepting an authorization response from a swapped issuer. In SDK v2 it is the client's finishAuth.

perguntas.p: A token with only turmas:ler tries reservar_vaga. What is the response?
opcoes: It books the seat, because it passed the gate
It asks the user for confirmation
perguntas.explica: The token is valid (it passes the server's gate), but the tool requires turmas:reservar. The SDK responds 403 before running the handler.

itens.texto: The MCP server checks the token; the IdP issues it.
Minimal, per tool, with a 403 when it is missing.
In the environment, never in the repository; audience checked.

links.t: SDK v2: require authorization on the server
RFC 9207: issuer identification in the authorization response
